newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: GOLF-WOOSNAM WINS SECOND TITLE IN A WEEK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM WINS SECOND TITLE IN A WEEK.

text.p: Ian Woosnam added the Hyundai Motor Masters title to the British PGA championship he won last Monday by beating fellow Briton Sandy Lyle on the second hole of a sudden death playoff on Sunday.
The Welshman converted a 15-foot birdie putt on the second extra holew after he and Lyle had finished the regulation 72 holes in 280, eight under par. Woosnam shot a final round of 68 to Lyle's 69.
For the second time this week heavy rain and lightning caused play to be suspended after the leaders had completed six holes with Lyle leading by one.

Overnight leader Choi Kyoung-ju of South Korea began with a bogey and a double bogey to lose his lead. He eventually finished joint fourth with Yasuharu Imano of Japan, one stroke behind third-placed Chung Jun of South Korea and five behind the leaders.
Woosnam's win earned him $90,000. "It's been hard work trying to cope with the conditions but fortunately it all came right in the end," he said.
Woosnam was impressed with Lyle, like himself a former U.S. Masters champion. "On his performance this week I'm sure he will win again very soon," Woosnam said.
